target_name: Total Shareholder Payout Against Hidden Research Capital
rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the archive's "Signed Payout Scaled by Hidden Research Capital" (identical hidden-capital leg, identical (prstkc+dvc-sstk)/at payout leg) with only the RANK-vs-ZSCORE transform changed, and it also sits one small term (dvc) away from "Off-Balance-Sheet Knowledge Capital Meets Buybacks" — a transform-level variant rather than a new mechanism.

The construction is internally coherent and correctly signed, but it is essentially an equal-weight average of the second legs of two already-tested archive signals sharing the same hidden-capital first leg, so it is a signal-blending exercise whose likely outcome (slope from the payout leg, alpha from the leverage leg) is already knowable from the archive rather than a new economic test.

The diagnosis of why the earlier bounded-ratio version returned NaN alphas is sound and the fix is legitimate, but a five-year cumulative issuance measure scaled by assets is very close to the published composite-issuance / net-external-financing anomaly, and subtracting cumulative R&D also loads it on the known R&D-intensity effect, so a positive result would be hard to distinguish from a repackaging of two documented anomalies.

Shifting from the stale intangible *level* to the year the intangible base expands on net new borrowing is a genuinely different economic event, the expression matches the hypothesis and sign, though the tester should check how much of it is absorbed by generic asset-growth and debt-issuance effects and note that DELTA of a ratio can be contaminated by denominator growth.

target_name: Full Debt Service Squeeze on Research Programs
rationale: This is a one-term hybrid of two existing archive signals (the best negative squeeze signal with dltr simply added into the dlc leg), which is close to a cosmetic variant; it also risks weakening the mechanism because dltr reflects routine refinancing capacity for healthy borrowers as much as cash drained from the lab.

This is a mechanical long-short ensemble of two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content, and because both components' first leg is R&D intensity the difference largely cancels the intangible exposure and reduces to a financing-direction score among research-heavy firms — i.e., the idea already covered by other proposals here.
